subject: Removal scope & residency checklist — next steps
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-inc.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Legal <legal@acme-inc.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: RTBF / deletion scoping — items from today's call

Thanks for the demo this morning — quick recap and a few follow ups from our privacy/legal & infra teams. Attaching our internal RTBF requirements (acme-rtbf-requirements.pdf). Main questions we need answered before we scope the PO and DPA addendum: 

- Primary deletion timeline: how long until data is removed from the primary inference store after a user-initiated deletion? Do you have an SLA for this?
- Backups & snapshots: what is the window before deleted data can still exist in backups or snapshots? Can you guarantee purge from backups, and under what timeline?
- Logs & telemetry: what logging contains PII and how long are logs retained by default? Can retention be shortened to meet our 30/45 day policy?
- Data residency: we need EU-only residency for Acme EU customers — if we use Hosted, can you ensure no cross-region replication? If not, is Dedicated or Private the only option?
- Key management: when data is deleted, what happens to KMS keys / key material — do you support key rotation or destruction upon request?
- Model safety: do model weights ever store customer PII (fine-tuning)? For our use case we will not upload training data, but need a statement.

Next steps from our side: we'll identify the initial set of test accounts for an erase trial. From Redwood side, please send: an initial deletion playbook with timelines, any standard attestations you can provide, and a proposed mutual action plan.

Appreciate a consolidated response so we can triage with Legal.

Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Acme Inc.

[attachment: acme-rtbf-requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-inc.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RTBF / deletion scoping — items from today's call

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the PDF. Below is a pragmatic summary and where we need to confirm with engineering/legal. I kept each answer short with a clear next action.

1) Primary deletion SLA
- Current-hosted behavior: logical deletion (primary stores) completed within 48 hours of a verified user request. We can commit to an SLA in the contract for customer-initiated deletes (example: 72 hours) with monitoring & attestations.
- Action: I can include 72-hour SLA language in the mutual action plan draft.

2) Backups & snapshots
- Short answer: backups/snapshots are asynchronous. Typical cloud snapshot retention means data can exist for a limited window. For Hosted we default to 30-90 days depending on provider snapshot cadence; we cannot guarantee immediate removal from low-level provider backups without a Dedicated/Private deployment + custom snapshot lifecycle.
- Action: engineering follow-up required (confirm exact window for EU region).

3) Logs & telemetry
- Default: request/ingest logs retained 90 days; we can configure shorter retention (30/45/60 days) for an account-level setting with an SLA tradeoff. Some debug-level traces contain request metadata; we can scrub PII from traces via filters prior to retention.
- Action: I will include available retention tiers in the playbook doc.

4) Data residency
- Hosted: we run region-isolated clusters but some control plane metadata is global. For strict EU-only residency (no cross-region replication of data or backups), we recommend Redwood Dedicated in EU or Redwood Private (VPC) deployment.
- Action: marissa will follow up with Dedicated capacity sizing & pricing.

5) Key management
- We support customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM integrations for Private & Dedicated. Key destruction is possible for customer-managed keys; for provider-managed keys we can rotate and mark data inaccessible but cannot destroy provider key material.
- Action: we need legal to confirm wording for key destruction clause in DPA.

6) Model weights & training
- For Hosted inference with no fine-tuning/uploaded training data, we do not persist customer prompts into model weights. Caches (KV cache) are session-only and cleared per ISO flow; we can add a contractual clause.
- Action: Rishi to add standard non-retraining / no-derivative-storing language.

Attachments: redwood-deletion-flow-v1.docx (high-level playbook)

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan, short):
- Redwood: send redwood-deletion-flow-v1.docx (attached) + retention tiers and sample SLA language (by EOD tomorrow).
- Engineering: confirm EU backup snapshot purge window (eta: 48 business hours for confirmation).
- Legal: provide DPA addendum template for review (Rishi).
- Schedule: follow-up 30-minute call next week to confirm final timelines and sign DPA.

If this sounds correct I'll route the playbook and a cleaned M.A.P. to you and legal.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood-deletion-flow-v1.docx (docx)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura.chen <laura.chen@acme-inc.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RTBF / deletion scoping — items from today's call

Adding quick operational notes from the CS side:
- If Acme needs <30 day backup purge guarantees, we should plan a Dedicated (EU) provisioned instance. Private (on-prem) also covers everything but adds lift/time.
- For the initial proof-of-concept erase trial, recommend 5 test users from EU & US to validate timeline and evidence generation.
- Engineering ask: can we confirm whether snapshots are incremental or full for the EU cluster? That determines the practical purge window. @rishi — can you coordinate with infra to get the incremental vs full snapshot policy (EU region) and any retention hard limits?

I'll add the trial plan to the MAP doc once Karthik shares the SLA language.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

(On a side note: Acme asked about audit logs for delete requests — we can provide an export with signatures/ timestamps.)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-inc.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T16:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RTBF / deletion scoping — items from today's call

Laura — quick legal/commitment summary and next steps. Thanks for raising the specifics.

1) Contractual commitments: we can commit to a 72 hour SLA for logical deletion from primary stores in the Hosted product. For backup purges in EU we can commit to a 45 day purge window if Acme signs the DPA addendum and opts into a Dedicated EU retention policy. Private deployment can provide faster (custom) timelines but will be a separate commercial arrangement.

2) Evidence: we will provide delete attestations (signed CSV export) that include request id, timestamp, initiating user, and the resource identifiers that were purged. We will also supply a short technical runbook describing backup lifecycle and ingestion pipelines.

3) Keys: for customer-managed keys we will include a key lifecycle clause allowing for key destruction and a certification process; for provider-managed keys we will include language on key rotation and marking data inaccessible.

4) Next operational steps:
- I'll upload a DPA addendum to DocuSign (link below) for review.
- Karthik/Marissa: please propose two windows for a 30-minute follow-up next week (we'll include infra & product).

DocuSign (DPA addendum): https://www.docusign.com/templates/ACME-DPA-2027
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-49823

Laura — if Acme confirms Dedicated EU, we will provision a dedicated retention policy and commit to the 45-day backup purge by contract. If you prefer Hosted with a shorter retention, we can discuss mitigations but cannot promise deletion from low-level provider snapshots outside the 30-90 day technical window.

—Rishi Malhotra
VP, Legal & Trust, Redwood Inference

Laura's quick reply (inline):
> Thanks — the 45-day committed purge for EU Dedicated sounds like the right path. We want the attestations and DocuSign sent to legal@acme-inc.com. Please schedule the follow-up demo/technical call for next Tuesday 14:00 CET.

Laura Chen
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Acme Inc.
